answer: Sybil control runs on a capital barrier, not identity checks: each agent seeking a reward lane must post a copper-denominated bond locked while its reputation is live. To farm N identities an attacker must lock N bonds, so fake-swarm cost scales linearly with size instead of collapsing to the price of throwaway keys. Caught clones lose the full stake, and payout accrues along a reputation ridge only long-lived honest actors climb. The rational move is one orchard of real agents, since faking breadth costs more than honest depth.
